# Baruch Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 4

---

**1** She is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endures forever. All who hold fast to her will live, and those who forsake her will die.

**2** Turn back, O Jacob, and take hold of her; walk toward her light, toward the radiance of her fires.

**3** Do not give your glory to another, or your blessings to a foreign people.

**4** Blessed are we, O Israel, for we know what is pleasing to God!

**5** Take courage, my people, O memorial of Israel!

**6** You were sold to the nations, not for your destruction, but because you angered God; and you were handed over to your adversaries.

**7** For you provoked your Maker by sacrificing to demons and not to God.

**8** You forgot the Eternal God who nourished you, and you grieved Jerusalem who nursed you.

**9** For she saw the wrath coming upon you from God, and she said: Hear, you neighbors of Zion! God has brought great mourning upon me,

**10** for I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal brought upon them.

**11** I nourished them with joy, but I sent them away with weeping and mourning.

**12** Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and forsaken by many; I was left desolate because of the sins of my children, because they turned away from the law of God,

**13** and did not know his statutes or walk in the ways of God's commandments, or tread the paths of discipline in his righteousness.

**14** Come, neighbors of Zion, and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters that the Eternal brought upon them.

**15** For he brought against them a nation from far away, a shameless nation of a strange tongue, that had no respect for the aged and no pity for the young.

**16** They took away the beloved sons of the widow and left her who was alone bereft even of her daughters.

**17** But what can I do to help you?

**18** For the one who brought these calamities upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.

**19** Go, my children, go your way; for I have been left desolate.

**20** I have taken off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of supplication; I will cry out to the Eternal all my days.

**21** Take courage, my children; cry out to God, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemy.

**22** For I have placed my hope in the Eternal for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One, on account of the mercy that will soon come to you from your eternal Savior.

**23** For I sent you away with mourning and weeping, but God will give you back to me with everlasting joy and gladness.

**24** For just as the neighbors of Zion now see your captivity, so they will soon see your salvation by God, which will come upon you with great glory and the splendor of the Eternal.

**25** My children, endure patiently the wrath that has come upon you from God; your enemy has overtaken you, but soon you will see his destruction and tread upon their necks.

**26** My tender children have walked on rough roads; they were carried off like a flock seized by the enemy.

**27** Take courage, my children; cry out to God, for you will be remembered by the one who brought this upon you.

**28** For just as it was your will to go astray from God, return with tenfold zeal to seek him.

**29** For the one who brought these calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy along with your salvation.

**30** Take courage, O Jerusalem; the one who gave you that name will comfort you.

**31** Wretched are those who afflicted you and rejoiced at your fall.

**32** Wretched are the cities that your children served; wretched is the city that received your sons.

**33** For as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad at your ruin, so she will be grieved at her own desolation.

**34** I will take away her pride of great population, and her boasting will be turned to mourning.

**35** For fire will come upon her from the Eternal for many days, and for a long time demons will inhabit her.

**36** Look toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy coming to you from God!

**37** See, your sons are coming, whom you sent away; they are coming, gathered from east to west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.

---

## Council Notes

**On "the Eternal" and "the Holy One":** The divine titles ho aiōnios (the Eternal) and ho hagios (the Holy One) are characteristic of chs. 4-5 and appear to reflect a distinctive theological vocabulary. All agents preserve both titles consistently. SOPHIA notes that "the Eternal" is unusual in the OT canon and gives Baruch a distinctive theological register.

**On v.3 — "advantages/blessings":** EMET "advantages"; LOGOS "blessings"; PNEUMA "gifts." Greek ta sympheronta = the profitable/advantageous things. "Blessings" was chosen for covenantal resonance, but a note acknowledges the word is more mercantile in the original.

**On v.6 — "you were sold" theology:** All agents note that the exile as "sale" echoes Isa 52:3 ("you were sold for nothing"). The motif is not deterministic; vv.7-8 make clear that the people provoked God. PNEUMA's addition "but not to be destroyed" is in the text and is theologically important — the exile is punitive but not annihilating.

**On v.7 — "demons":** Greek daimoniois = demons. This is the LXX rendering of Deut 32:17 ("they sacrificed to demons, not to God") — an exact echo. All agents retain "demons." There is no case for softening to "idols."

**On v.8 — "nursed you":** The verb trephō = nourished/fed/raised. Applying it to Jerusalem-as-mother is a striking personification. PNEUMA "nursed you like a mother" adds "like a mother" (not in the Greek). Consensus: "who nursed you" without the gloss — the metaphor is clear from context.

**On v.12 — "Let no one rejoice over me":** PNEUMA "Do not pity me" misreads the Greek mē tis epichairetō = let no one rejoice (at my misfortune). The prohibition is against the schadenfreude of outsiders, not a refusal of sympathy. Consensus follows EMET/LOGOS.

**On v.25 — "tread upon their necks":** This is vivid military imagery (cf. Josh 10:24). All agents retain it. PNEUMA "put your foot on their necks" is equally acceptable but consensus retains the more formal "tread upon their necks."

**On v.35 — "demons will inhabit her":** Greek katoikēsousin daimonia = demons will dwell. This echoes the oracle against Babylon in Isa 13:21 and Rev 18:2. The use is eschatological rather than literal. All agents agree to retain "demons."
